analysis_notes.source_text_structure: This is a short mashal-based teaching (6 sentences). It is built entirely from eitza (cause-and-effect) and analogy (mashal/nimshal). The word 'בְּחִינַת' does not appear anywhere in the Torah text. The teaching has the following causal chain: (1) All hashpa'ot come only from the Tzaddik ha-Emet. (2) Each person receives through their Mazal. (3) The Mazal receives from the Tzaddik. (4) Distant from Tzaddik → Mazal must exert great force → risk of death or loss. (5) Close to Tzaddik → Mazal exerts no force → smooth flow. (6) Sometimes closeness to Tzaddik causes loss of wealth: the Mazal sees something more precious (the Tzaddik's light) and discards the material wealth — analogous to a porter carrying copper who sees gold and gems and drops everything. (7) Even more so: when the person himself appreciates the closeness, he does not care for wealth at all. The Talmudic citation (Megillah 3: דְּאִיהוּ לָא חָזֵי מַזְלֵהּ חָזֵי — 'he himself does not see but his Mazal sees') is used as supporting evidence for mechanism (6), not as a bechina equation.

dataset_edge_for_this_torah.classification_verdict: Correctly classified as eitza. Closeness to the Tzaddik PRODUCES easy receiving — one thing causes the other. This is not a bechina (they are not two expressions of the same underlying nature).

analysis_notes.package_creation_verdict: NO PACKAGES POSSIBLE from bechina subgraph because no bechina edges exist. The Torah's conceptual work is done entirely through eitza chains and mashal. It does not establish identity-of-nature between concepts — it establishes causal pathways. If packages were ever to be built for this Torah, they would need to be sourced from cross-Torah bechina connections that happen to include the key nodes (e.g., מַזָּל, הַשְׁפָּעָה, צַדִּיק) appearing in other Torahs, but those would be different Torah-specific packages, not Torah #240 packages.
